Although the AirPods equipped with cameras are not expected to launch until next year, a Bloomberg report indicates that Apple may unveil AirPods 5 early at next month's iPhone event. Here are the relevant details.

AirPods 5 will come in standard and Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) versions

In a wide-ranging report published earlier this evening, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said Apple could announce a new Mac mini in the coming days, earlier than the September event he had anticipated.

Gurman also detailed several other products Apple has in the pipeline, including AirPods 5, which could debut as soon as next month. He said the company's next expected event will be held on September 9, where it will also unveil its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro series, and new Apple Watch models.

The report reads as follows:

The company is also preparing a series of modest Apple Watch updates, including fitness tracking upgrades and a ceramic case option for the Series 12 model. It is also planning to launch new AirPods as early as the September product event. Sources said the new lineup will include AirPods 5, an update to Apple's entry-level earbuds. The previous model was refreshed in 2024. As for the version with cameras, that is not expected until next year.

Interestingly, following his own report, Gurman posted a follow-up on social platform X, adding that AirPods 5 is expected to launch in both standard and noise-cancelling versions:

Although there has been limited information about the AirPods 5 timeline, industry consensus generally expected these earbuds wouldn't arrive until 2027. Apple is also reportedly developing two AirPods models with cameras, which will offer AI features through Visual Intelligence and Siri.

Apple earlier mistakenly included a demo video of camera-equipped AirPods in the macOS 26.7 candidate release, though the clip didn't clearly show any visual differences for the device.
